tasks.short: Turn the board's budget guidelines into budget instructions, templates and rules for site and cost-centre managers.

today.trigger: The Finance Director passes on the board's budget framework (in September), or the bank or board changes targets in the middle of the year.
steps: Read the board memo and the bank covenant terms, and note the targets: EBITDA, headcount, capex ceiling.
Translate the CAO wage rounds, flex worker rates and indexation into planning assumptions.
Write the budget instruction and update the Excel templates for each site and cost centre on SharePoint.
Answer managers' questions by mail and in Teams, and keep a list of exceptions.
Check the submitted budgets against the rules by hand.
drudgery: Rewriting last year's instruction document line by line
Answering the same questions from managers on three sites
Checking by hand whether submissions follow the rules
today.time_sinks: Questions from managers and checking submissions take more time than writing the policy.

lenses.faster: A model drafts the instruction and the assumptions table from the board memo, the CAO texts and last year's version, and a rule check flags submissions that break the rules; the analyst edits and decides, so about a quarter of the time goes.
lenses.autonomous: When a new board framework lands on SharePoint, a draft instruction and a list of what changed from last year are produced; nothing goes to managers until the analyst and the Finance Director approve.
lenses.ambitious: A new service for site managers: a Teams Q&A bot that answers from the approved budget instruction only, so managers on night and weekend shifts in Venlo get answers outside office hours; demand would grow if it were cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss rewriting the template or answering the same flex-rate question twenty times; the analyst wants more time on the judgement calls about which exceptions to allow.
lenses.options: Draft two or three versions of a rule (for example a hard headcount cap against a cost envelope per site) with their effect on last year's numbers, so the Finance Director chooses knowing the trade-off.
lenses.altitude: The analyst moves from writing documents to owning the planning assumptions and deciding on exceptions with the Controller, which makes the job more expert.
reach: Controller: keeping the chart of accounts and cost-centre mapping in line with budget rules (needs to learn AFAS ledger setup)
HR Business Partner: headcount assumptions per site (needs CAO pay scale knowledge)

tasks.human_edge: Reading what the board and the bank really want, judging which exceptions a site manager deserves, and handling the politics between sites cannot be handed over.
tasks.pattern_why: Setting policy is a judgement call; the model drafts text and comparisons, and a plain rule check on submissions can be written as deterministic software.

in_practice.trigger: Board budget framework or a mid-year change in targets is saved to the Finance SharePoint folder.
steps: Model compares the new framework with last year's instruction and lists what changed.
Model drafts the instruction text and the assumptions table (CAO wage rounds, flex rates, indexation) with a source for each number.
Analyst edits, picks between rule options and gets the Finance Director's approval.
Deterministic check validates the submitted Excel budgets against the rules and lists the breaches.
in_practice.human_gate: The Finance Director signs off the instruction before managers see it; the analyst decides on every exception.
systems: Microsoft 365 Copilot or an approved company LLM
data_needed: Board budget framework and bank covenant terms
in_practice.logs_to: Versioned instruction and exception log in the Finance SharePoint library

evidence.claim: Finance executives found AI more useful than expected for budgeting (+42 net), least where human judgement is needed.
Agents do not fix undefined drivers and unencoded policies; speed makes existing errors harder to catch.
Drafting policy text from source documents is a routine LLM capability.

risks: A draft that misreads a CAO clause goes into every site's budget
Managers treat the bot's answer as policy when it was never approved
Old rules get carried forward without anyone questioning them
research_questions: How many manager questions per budget round are repeats that an approved Q&A could answer?
How many submitted budgets broke a rule last year, and how many breaches were found late?
Does the Finance Director accept a model-drafted instruction if every number shows its source?

tasks.short: Build business cases: lease or buy forklifts, flex or permanent staff, site investments, financing options with Rabobank.

today.trigger: A site manager, the Finance Director or the board asks for an investment or staffing decision, or a funding request comes in.
steps: Gather costs from AFAS, agency invoices, supplier quotes and lease offers.
Build an Excel model with NPV, payback and sensitivities.
Check assumptions with operations, HR (CAO costs) and the Controller.
Write a memo and a PowerPoint for the decision meeting.
drudgery: Pulling agency hours and rates from three portals
Rebuilding the same NPV structure for each case
today.time_sinks: Collecting and cleaning input data and rebuilding models each time.

lenses.faster: A standard model template with fixed formulas, data pulled automatically from AFAS and the agency portals, and a model-drafted memo cut the build from days to hours; the analyst still checks the assumptions and the story, so about 40% of the time goes.
lenses.autonomous: A funding request on the SharePoint form starts a pre-filled case with the data and a draft memo; it only counts once the analyst has checked it and the Finance Director decides.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: the flex-or-permanent comparison per site and per season, run every quarter instead of once a year, so HR and site managers hire on numbers; demand would grow as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss copying agency invoice lines into Excel; the analyst wants more time testing assumptions with the operations managers.
lenses.options: Show three scenarios (base, high volume, loss of a large customer) and two financing options side by side, because the choice between lease and buy often flips between scenarios.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the business-case standard and the hurdle rates and advises at the decision meeting instead of assembling spreadsheets; the job becomes more expert.
reach: Controller: lease accounting treatment of the options (needs to learn IFRS 16 or Dutch GAAP lease rules)
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: full employee cost under the CAO for flex-or-permanent cases

tasks.human_edge: Choosing realistic assumptions, sensing what operations will really deliver, and defending the case in front of the board and the bank remain human work.
tasks.pattern_why: The arithmetic can be fixed in a template, but which options to compare and which assumptions hold need the analyst's judgement; the digest puts cost-benefit at copilot with options.

in_practice.trigger: A funding or investment request is filed on the SharePoint request form.
steps: Deterministic template pulls costs from AFAS and hours and rates from the agency portal exports.
Template calculates NPV, payback and sensitivities for each scenario.
Model drafts the memo with options and lists the assumptions that have no source.
Analyst checks the assumptions with operations and HR and finalises the recommendation.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst signs off the model and the memo; the Finance Director or the board decides.
systems: Microsoft 365 Copilot or an approved company LLM
data_needed: AFAS cost and payroll data by cost centre
Hurdle rate and financing terms from Rabobank
in_practice.logs_to: Business-case library on SharePoint, with model version and assumptions sheet

evidence.claim: Finance executives report net gains from AI in model building (+27) and scenario planning (+26).
FP&A agents run scenario mechanics and draft commentary while people decide on capital allocation.
Workpapers built in personal chatbots cannot be rebuilt for the auditor.

risks: Agency data is mapped inconsistently across the three portals
Cases are built in personal chat tools and cannot be traced
research_questions: How many business cases a year are built, and how many hours does data gathering take per case?
Can the three agency portals export hours and rates in a stable format?
Would HR and site managers act on a quarterly flex-or-permanent comparison?

tasks.short: Look for cost savings and margin improvements across sites, flex labour, transport and customers.

today.trigger: The monthly results review, a margin drop at a site or customer, or a cost-saving target from the board.
steps: Pull cost, revenue and hours data from Power BI and AFAS.
Compare sites, customers and cost per order line or per pallet.
Look for outliers: overtime, agency premiums, absence costs, unprofitable contracts.
Discuss findings with site managers and present ideas to the Finance Director.
drudgery: Building the same site comparisons in Excel each month
Matching agency invoices to booked hours by hand
today.time_sinks: Finding the outliers takes most of the time, leaving little time to work out causes with operations.

lenses.faster: Fixed checks run every night on the AFAS extract (agency rate against contract, overtime against plan, margin per customer) and a model writes a short list of candidates with the source data; the analyst still investigates causes, so about a quarter of the time goes.
lenses.autonomous: Each nightly refresh runs the checks and posts new outliers to a Teams channel; nothing becomes a savings proposal without the analyst.
lenses.ambitious: A new service for the three site managers: a monthly margin and productivity pack for each site and customer, with the top three improvement candidates; demand would grow if it were cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss matching agency invoices line by line; the analyst wants more time on the warehouse floor and with operations working out why a site is behind.
lenses.options: For each candidate saving, show several moves (renegotiate the agency rate, change shift patterns, reprice the customer) with their effect, because the right lever differs per site.
lenses.altitude: The analyst becomes the site managers' sparring partner on margin, decides which candidates get pursued and tracks realised savings; the job becomes more expert.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: spotting customers whose margin and payment behaviour both get worse (needs to learn DSO and credit limit rules)
Bookkeeper: checking agency invoices against contracted rates (needs to learn the agency contract terms)

tasks.human_edge: Knowing the operation, the customers and the people well enough to tell a real saving from a number artefact, and persuading site managers, needs a person.
tasks.pattern_why: The outlier checks are deterministic, but choosing and pursuing improvements is open-ended judgement that the analyst leads.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly Power BI refresh of the AFAS extract, plus the monthly results review.
steps: Deterministic checks compare agency rates, overtime, absence costs and customer margins against contract and plan.
Model summarises the new outliers, with links to the underlying lines, into a short candidate list.
Analyst investigates the causes with site managers and drops false alarms.
Analyst presents the chosen proposals with options to the Finance Director and tracks what is realised.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst decides which candidates become proposals; the Finance Director approves actions.
data_needed: AFAS cost, revenue and hours by site and customer
Volume drivers per site (order lines, pallets)
Absence data, aggregated with no named people (AVG)
in_practice.logs_to: Savings tracker on SharePoint with source links and status

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI can summarise reports and answer questions, but needs a prepared semantic model and Fabric F2+ or Premium capacity; non-English use is not officially supported.
FP&A agents flag records that do not tie and monitor variances; people decide what to act on.
Data quality is the top barrier to AI in finance (40.4%).

risks: Too many false alarms and the channel gets ignored
Cost per pallet is defined differently at each site, so comparisons mislead
Absence or overtime data on named people is processed without a lawful basis or works council consent (AVG, OR right of consent on monitoring)
research_questions: Are volume drivers (order lines, pallets) available per site in AFAS or the warehouse system?
How many agency invoice lines last year differed from the contracted rate, and by how much?
Would site managers use a monthly margin pack, and what would they act on?

role.altitude: The FP&A analyst stops assembling budgets and business cases and owns the drivers, definitions and forecast rules: the planning assumptions, the business-case standard and the margin checks that site managers and the Finance Director rely on.
reach: Controller: cost-centre mapping and lease accounting for business cases
HR Business Partner and Compensation and Benefits Specialist: headcount and CAO cost assumptions
Bookkeeper: checking agency invoices against contracted rates
Credit and Collections Officer: combined margin and payment-risk view per customer
role.ceiling_note: The work is limited by data quality and definitions (a nightly AFAS extract, three agency portals, drivers per site not yet defined), by Power BI Copilot's need for a prepared model, capacity and English, and by board, bank and works council conversations that stay human; on these three tasks roughly a quarter to two fifths of the time can go.
skills_to_grow: Defining drivers and the semantic model in Power BI
Writing rule checks and templates with AI coding help
Data protection (AVG) and works council rules for workforce data
Prompting and checking LLM drafts with sources
role.ambitious_version: Run monthly rolling forecasts and scenarios for each site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo) and each large customer, with a quarterly flex-or-permanent comparison and a margin pack for site managers, once the drivers are defined and certified.
